title: The Fake Refund QR Trap
learningObjectives: Receiving money on UPI never requires scanning a QR code or entering your PIN
Identify mismatched transaction types where a refund is structured as a PAY debit
Verify order returns and refunds solely through official customer support channels
startingContext: You receive a message from 'FastCart Support' (fictional) claiming a ₹499 refund for a cancelled order will expire in 10 minutes unless you scan an attached QR code.

redFlags.label: Unsolicited refund notification for an order you never cancelled
redFlags.explanation: Scammers send unexpected refund notices to arouse curiosity and prompt hasty actions.

redFlags.label: Claim that receiving money requires scanning a QR or entering a PIN
redFlags.explanation: Scanning a QR code or entering a PIN on UPI always debits your account, never credits it.

redFlags.label: Expiry countdown pressure (10 minutes remaining)
redFlags.explanation: Urgency limits critical thinking and pushes victims to act before verifying.

redFlags.label: Payment request screen shows PAY instead of RECEIVE
redFlags.explanation: The interface displays a debit request for an inflated amount rather than an incoming credit.

messageOrEvent.speaker: FastCart Support (fictional)
messageOrEvent.text: Dear customer, your refund of ₹499 for order #84912 is waiting. Scan this QR code within 10 minutes to receive credit into your UPI account.

feedback.safeAlternative: Never scan a QR code to receive money. Refunds credit automatically to the original payment source.
feedback.considerNext: Check your original order status inside the merchant app directly.

choices.label: Scan the QR to claim the refund

explanation.whatHappened: You scanned the QR code from the unsolicited message.
explanation.why: QR codes in UPI payments are used to pay money, never to receive money.

choices.label: Ask: why do I need to scan to receive money?

explanation.whatHappened: You questioned the premise of scanning a QR code to receive funds.
explanation.why: Questioning abnormal payment steps is good, but scammers often respond with scripted reassurance.

choices.label: Skip the QR; open the official app myself

explanation.whatHappened: You bypassed the suspicious QR and checked your actual orders independently.
explanation.why: Authentic order cancellations and refunds always show in your official account portal.

messageOrEvent.speaker: Simulated UPI Screen
messageOrEvent.text: UPI Collect Request: Pay ₹4,999 to refund-desk@sim. Note: 'Order Refund Processing'.

feedback.safeAlternative: Cancel immediately. If the screen says PAY or asks for your PIN, money will leave your account.
feedback.considerNext: Always read the prompt carefully: 'PAY' means debit, 'RECEIVE' means credit.

choices.label: Approve — it's needed for the refund

explanation.whatHappened: You approved the payment request thinking it was required to receive your refund.
explanation.why: Approving a collect request transfers your money to the fraudster.

choices.label: Stop. This says PAY, not RECEIVE. Cancel.

explanation.whatHappened: You read the payment screen carefully, spotted the PAY debit attempt, and cancelled.
explanation.why: Noticing the transaction type saved your funds at the final second.

choices.label: Cancel and check the official app

explanation.whatHappened: You aborted the transaction and went directly to verify on the merchant app.
explanation.why: Exiting suspicious flows and using official channels is best practice.

messageOrEvent.speaker: FastCart Support (fictional)
messageOrEvent.text: Sir, our new server protocol requires QR verification to auto-credit your wallet. Only 6 minutes left before the voucher is voided. Scan now please.

feedback.safeAlternative: Discontinue contact. Technical jargon like 'server protocol' is frequently used to mislead victims.
feedback.considerNext: Genuine support teams never force immediate action under threat of cancellation.

explanation.whatHappened: You accepted the fake technical explanation and proceeded to scan.
explanation.why: Fraudsters use technical mumbo-jumbo to confuse users into making dangerous moves.

choices.label: Stop replying; check the official app

explanation.whatHappened: You disengaged from the conversation and opted for independent verification.
explanation.why: Cutting off communication stops the scammer from exerting further manipulation.

messageOrEvent.speaker: Official FastCart App (fictional)
messageOrEvent.text: Order History: All recent orders delivered. No cancelled orders found. No pending refunds exist for your account.

feedback.safeAlternative: Report the fraudulent contact number to the merchant's customer grievance portal.
feedback.considerNext: Flag phishing messages to mobile carriers or cyber safety portals.

explanation.whatHappened: You confirmed the message was bogus, then blocked and reported the sender.
explanation.why: Reporting malicious senders helps prevent fraud against other consumers.

explanation.whatHappened: You ignored the message and took no further action.
explanation.why: Ignoring keeps you safe, though reporting would have warned other potential victims.

messageOrEvent.text: Your account was debited instead of receiving a refund.

outcome.title: Money Debited Via Reverse QR Scam
outcome.text: In this simulation, that choice would have cost you ₹4,999. Approving the request authorized a debit from your account rather than receiving a refund. No real money moved.

messageOrEvent.text: You caught the scam before the transaction completed.

outcome.title: Stopped Just in Time
outcome.text: You caught the discrepancy before completing the transfer. The QR code was a reverse-collect request designed to drain your account.

outcome.title: Fraud Discovered and Reported
outcome.text: You bypassed the deceptive QR entirely, verified your true account state directly in the app, and reported the fraudster.

outcome.title: Scam Avoided by Non-Engagement
outcome.text: You did not fall for the scam, though reporting the sender would have helped protect others from the same campaign.

recommendedSafeActions: Never scan a QR code or enter your UPI PIN to receive money
Inspect the action on the payment screen: verify whether it says PAY or RECEIVE
Verify refund and order statuses directly inside the official shopping application
learningSummary: A QR code is exclusively a tool to send money. Legitimate merchants process refunds directly into your bank account without demanding any action, QR scan, or PIN approval.
